tfn.s: AP-NORC asked 1,182 adults about their film habits in August 2025.
tfn.why: The text says: "AP-NORC asked 1,182 adults in August 2025 about their film habits."

tfn.s: European cinemas sold more tickets in 2025 than in the year before.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "That is fewer than the year before, but it is still an enormous number of people choosing to leave the house for a film."

tfn.s: Cinema tickets cost more now than they did ten years ago.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text says cinema tickets are bought one at a time, but it gives no prices from the past.

tfn.s: The British Film Institute found that younger adults valued the cinema as a place where they actually watch.
tfn.why: The text says: "Research by the British Film Institute in 2025 found that younger adults valued the cinema partly because it is a place where they actually watch, without checking a phone."

tfn.s: Plenty of people stream most weeks and never go to the cinema.

focus.note: Small words join ideas. Because gives a reason, but shows a contrast, so shows a result and while means at the same time.

tfn.s: A family of four may spend more on one cinema evening than on a month of streaming.
tfn.why: The text says an ordinary evening out "can cost more than a month of watching at home".

tfn.s: Higher earners in the AP-NORC poll were less likely to have been to a cinema than lower earners.
tfn.why: 72% of those earning $100,000 or more had been, against 54% of those earning under $50,000.

tfn.s: Cinemas in Europe sold fewer tickets in 2025, but the money they took did not fall much.
tfn.why: Admissions fell by around 5.5%, "yet box office revenue stayed broadly level".

tfn.s: Most young adults in the UK said they preferred the cinema to watching at home.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text says they valued the cinema as a focused and social occasion, but gives no preference figures.

tfn.s: Worldwide takings in 2025 had returned to their pre-pandemic level.
tfn.why: They rose about 5% but "remained some 30% below the average before the pandemic".

tfn.s: The writer implies that cinemas can no longer rely on exclusive access to new films.
tfn.why: Access "was the thing it used to own outright", but the same film is now available both ways.

tfn.s: The BFI found that most young adults wanted cinemas to be more relaxed about phones.
tfn.why: Only 14% wanted venues to be more relaxed about talking or phones.

tfn.s: Global takings grew in 2025, yet were still lower than before the pandemic.
tfn.why: They "grew roughly 5%" but "still sat about 30% below their pre-pandemic average".

tfn.s: Streaming services now release more quiet films than big spectacles.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text only worries that quieter films may lose their route to an audience at cinemas.

tfn.s: The writer treats the AP-NORC results as proof that cinema is declining worldwide.
tfn.why: The poll "is American and measures frequency, so it cannot be stretched into a global judgement".

speak.title: Role-play: sofa or cinema?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: A new film is out on Friday. You want to see it on the big screen with your partner. Explain why it's worth the trip and the price. Try to agree a plan.

b.text: You'd rather stay in and stream a film. Say why, and ask what makes the cinema worth the money. You can say yes, no, or suggest a different plan.

phrases: I'd really like to see it on the big screen.
Is it worth the price of two tickets?
I'd rather stay in and stream it.
That's true, but we can't pause a film at the cinema.
What if we go this time and stream the next one?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you go out or stay in, and who gave up more?
